clue.text: All go in one gate to get into school?

definitions.text: All go in one gate to get into school?

parts.words: All go in one gate to get into school?
parts.note: read literally, a gate everyone shares is a shared way in; read as education, it is the exam taken to win a place at an independent school

explanation.surface: A question about how pupils are funnelled through a single school gate.
explanation.walkthrough: COMMON ENTRANCE is the exam British children sit, usually at 13, for entry to independent (fee-paying) senior schools; the surface pictures a literal shared gate.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a shared doorway, and also the name of the admission exam for private schools.

clue.text: Consigns company to get r-repairs

parts.note: the stammered spelling doubles the first letter, so 'repairs' (mends) is given with its first letter repeated: M-MENDS

explanation.surface: A firm hands work over to someone to have repairs done, the stutter suggesting a nervous speaker.
explanation.walkthrough: The hyphenated 'r-repairs' is a stutter: it tells you to repeat the first letter of the synonym, so MENDS becomes MMENDS.
explanation.definitionFit: To commend something is to entrust or hand it over, as in commending a soul to God.

clue.text: It's essential to overlook broken reed you'll have gathered

indicators.note: in a down clue, to overlook is to sit above, so this piece goes on top of the next

parts.note: 'it's essential' means you must, giving MUST

indicators.note: broken says the letters of reed are smashed and rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone notes that a broken reed must be ignored, as you'll have gathered.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Overlook' looks like 'ignore', but in a down clue it means 'sit above'; 'broken' makes ERED from the reed.
explanation.definitionFit: Troops mustered are troops assembled or brought together.

clue.text: Recently dwelling in Old English environment

indicators.note: environment means surroundings, so the Old English abbreviation surrounds the dwelling

parts.note: a flat is a dwelling

explanation.surface: A remark about someone living lately in an old-fashioned English setting.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dwelling in' reads as living somewhere, but 'environment' is what does the work: it means surroundings, so the abbreviation wraps round the home.
explanation.definitionFit: 'Of late' is a set phrase meaning lately, in the recent past.

clue.text: See 1
Standard size for short man

definitions.meaning: The shortened form of the man's name Norman

explanation.surface: Someone asks what counts as the standard size for a short man.
explanation.definitionFit: A norm is the expected standard, and Norm is a nickname for Norman.

clue.text: Peculiar wallop? No, mixed drink

parts.note: rum is old British slang for odd or peculiar
a wallop is a hard blow, a punch

explanation.surface: Someone corrects themselves: not the beer called wallop but a cocktail.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wallop' is also British slang for beer, so 'No, mixed drink' seems to reject it; really 'No' only links, and 'wallop' is the blow.
explanation.definitionFit: A cocktail of rum, fruit juice and spices is a classic blended beverage.

clue.text: Such people getting under car would be a bloomer

indicators.note: in a down clue, getting under the car means the answer sits below it, so the flower minus the car leaves the answer

parts.note: a bloomer is a flower, here the carnation

explanation.surface: Someone crawling under a car making a blunder, a bloomer.
explanation.walkthrough: Put the car above the answer and you get a flower: 'bloomer' here means something that blooms, not a blunder.
explanation.definitionFit: A nation is a people united by country and culture.

clue.text: Former building land said to cause stir

parts.note: ex means former, as in ex-wife

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken, so a word sounding like it is used

parts.note: a site is land for building on

explanation.surface: Old building land, reportedly, is causing a stir among locals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Said' turns SITE into its sound-alike CITE.
explanation.definitionFit: To excite is to rouse or stir up feeling.

clue.text: The strength provided by seafood one hears

indicators.note: one hears says the shellfish's name is spoken, giving a word that sounds the same

parts.note: a mussel is a shellfish eaten as seafood

explanation.surface: A claim that eating seafood gives you strength.
explanation.definitionFit: Muscle is used for physical power or force, as in 'putting some muscle into it'.

clue.text: A movement of 9 after wee drink is impressive

indicators.note: after places the preceding letters behind the small drink

parts.note: a dram is a small measure of whisky; wee is Scots for small
a tic is an involuntary twitch of the body tissue answered at clue 9

explanation.surface: A dance movement performed after a little whisky proves striking.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Movement' suggests music or dance, but with '9' it is a twitch of a muscle: a TIC.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dramatic is striking and makes a strong impression.

clue.text: Interruption to flow of work to be performed by one

definitions.text: Interruption to flow of work to be performed by one

parts.words: Interruption to flow of work to be performed by one
parts.note: in a concerto the orchestra stops and one soloist plays a showy passage alone, breaking the flow of the piece

explanation.surface: Seems to describe a hold-up in an office's workflow handled by one person.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is a musical composition, and 'one' is the soloist.
explanation.definitionFit: A solo virtuoso passage that pauses the orchestral music of a concerto.

clue.text: Last dance tune with valeta final couple missed

indicators.note: dance tells us to jig the letters about into a new order
the final couple of letters of valeta are dropped

explanation.surface: The last tune at a ballroom evening, a valeta, when the final couple failed to appear.
explanation.walkthrough: A valeta is an old-time ballroom dance. 'final couple missed' drops TA, leaving VALE, and 'dance' rearranges TUNE + VALE into the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Eventual means coming at the end, ultimate.

clue.text: Leave port, being offended

definitions.meaning: a ship sets sail from harbour

explanation.surface: A sailor leaving harbour in a huff.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship puts out to sea, and someone put out is annoyed.

clue.text: The sin of the receiver

parts.note: a fence is a criminal who receives stolen goods

explanation.surface: A moral judgement that receiving stolen goods is the sin.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Receiver' is the old legal term for a handler of stolen property, called a fence in slang.
explanation.definitionFit: A wrongdoing or transgression against law or morality.

clue.text: Tied around specially selected food

indicators.note: around tells us to turn the letters of tied about into another order

explanation.surface: A label tied round a package of chosen food.
explanation.definitionFit: A diet is a regime of food chosen for health or weight.

clue.text: Tense but immaculate

definitions.meaning: a grammatical tense, as in 'I have eaten'

explanation.surface: Someone nervous but flawlessly turned out.
explanation.definitionFit: The perfect tense shows completed action, and perfect means flawless.

clue.text: Leaves school for digs

definitions.meaning: in Britain a school ... when term ends and pupils go home
digs means breaks the soil apart

explanation.surface: A pupil leaves school to go to his lodgings, digs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Digs' looks like British slang for lodgings, but here it is the verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A British school ends its term, and digging splits the ground apart.

clue.text: Trust need pond to be redesigned

indicators.note: redesigned says the letters of need and pond are laid out in a new order

explanation.surface: A garden trust says it needs its pond redesigned.
explanation.definitionFit: To rely on someone is to put faith in them.

clue.text: Lady MC introduces first of comedians for a spot of business

indicators.note: introduces means the hostess takes something into her midst

parts.note: a commère is a female compère, the woman hosting a show

indicators.note: first of takes just the opening letter of comedians

explanation.surface: A hostess brings on the first comedian for a short routine.
explanation.walkthrough: COMMERE is the female form of compère, a master of ceremonies; 'introduces' puts C inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Commerce is trade, the buying and selling of goods.

clue.text: Official announcer demolished lightweight staff

indicators.note: demolished means ate up, so the announcer swallows the weight

parts.note: a town crier made public announcements
oz, the ounce, is a small unit of weight

explanation.surface: A public official has torn down a flimsy staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Demolished' means 'devoured', as in demolishing a plate of food: the announcer swallows the ounce.
explanation.definitionFit: A bishop's hooked ceremonial staff.

clue.text: Redecorate some ill-prepared offices

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Badly organised offices need doing up.
explanation.definitionFit: To redo a room is to decorate it afresh.

clue.text: Almost exact summary

indicators.note: almost means the synonym stops short of its last letter

parts.note: precise means exact

explanation.surface: A summary that is nearly accurate.
explanation.definitionFit: A précis is a condensed version of a text.

clue.text: Lady on river has that extra something

indicators.note: in a down clue, on means placed above the next piece

parts.note: Ann is a woman's name
the Exe is a river in Devon

explanation.surface: A woman by a river who has a certain charm.
explanation.walkthrough: 'That extra something' suggests charisma, but it is an extension to a building.
explanation.definitionFit: An annexe is an additional building added to a main one.

clue.text: Important document often seen in the tube?

definitions.text: Important document often seen in the tube?

parts.words: Important document often seen in the tube?
parts.note: a rolled parchment is kept in a cylindrical case, not on the Underground

explanation.surface: Seems to ask about papers read on the London Underground, the Tube.
explanation.walkthrough: The Tube is London's Underground railway, but here a tube is simply a cylinder that a rolled document sits in.
explanation.definitionFit: A rolled roll of parchment or paper bearing writing.

clue.text: Railwaymen returning to track where some journeys begin

indicators.note: returning says the union's initials are read backwards

parts.note: NUR was the National Union of Railwaymen
a way is a track or path

explanation.surface: Railway workers going back to the line where trips start.
explanation.definitionFit: Flights take off from an airfield's strip.

clue.text: After reordering rice came as the sweet

indicators.note: reordering says the letters of rice came are arranged afresh

explanation.surface: After rearranging dishes, rice came as dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: A frozen dessert, a sweet in British usage.

clue.text: Signify a change of name

indicators.note: a change of says the letters of name are altered into a new order

explanation.surface: To indicate that someone has changed their name.
explanation.definitionFit: To signify is to convey a meaning, to denote.

clue.text: The board will always support their moves

definitions.text: The board will always support their moves

parts.words: The board will always support their moves
parts.note: sounds like a company board backing executives, but the board is a chequered one and the pieces move on it

explanation.surface: A loyal company board that always backs its managers' decisions.
explanation.definitionFit: The pieces used to play the game of kings and pawns sit on the board.

clue.text: Pound for the talc?

definitions.meaning: to pound is to grind into fine particles
talc is a fine dust used on the skin

explanation.surface: A question about a pound's worth of talc.
explanation.definitionFit: Grinding reduces something to dust, and talc is a dusting dust.

clue.text: This gives a wide view at a stroke!

definitions.text: This gives a wide view at a stroke!

parts.words: This gives a wide view at a stroke!
parts.note: a single quick look that takes in a broad scene

explanation.surface: Seems to praise a device that shows a panorama instantly.
explanation.definitionFit: A quick look that takes in everything in a wide arc.

clue.text: See 30
